note: Non-state armed groups that historical events put on the map (docs/CONFLICTS_PLAN.md). Tags are three letters and must not be country tags. Colours and templates are gameplay choices, not facts.

groups.name: Islamic State
groups.description: Salafi jihadist militant organisation, also known as ISIL, ISIS or Da'esh. It held large parts of Iraq and Syria from 2014, proclaimed a caliphate that year, and lost its territory there by 2019.

groups.name: Taliban
groups.description: The Taliban insurgency began after the movement lost power in the 2001 war in Afghanistan. It fought the Afghan governments of Hamid Karzai and Ashraf Ghani and a US-led coalition; its 2021 offensive ended with the collapse of the Ghani government.

groups.name: Hamas
groups.description: The Islamic Resistance Movement, a Sunni Islamist Palestinian nationalist organisation with a military wing, the al-Qassam Brigades. Founded in 1987; it has governed the Gaza Strip since 2007.

groups.name: Donetsk People's Republic
groups.description: Proclaimed in 2014 by Russian-backed separatists who took control of part of Donetsk Oblast, starting the war in Donbas. It declared independence and was annexed by Russia in 2022.

groups.name: Luhansk People's Republic
groups.description: Proclaimed in 2014 by Russian-backed separatists who took control of part of Luhansk Oblast. It declared independence and was annexed by Russia in 2022.

groups.name: Syrian opposition
groups.description: Umbrella term for the groups that opposed the Ba'athist government in the Syrian civil war. Army defectors formed the Free Syrian Army in July 2011; by 2021 Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham was the strongest faction. Modelled here as one side.

groups.name: Hezbollah
groups.description: Lebanese Shia Islamist political party with a paramilitary wing, founded in 1982. Its armed wing fought Israel in the 2006 Lebanon war.
